THIS MFA HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 30.01.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is by the petitioner under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act'), seeking enhancement of the compensation for the injury sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident dated 17.06.2014.
2.
For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioner that on 17.06.2014, in order to go to Bank, he was proceeding on motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-36/V-3100 (for short 'motor cycle'), in a slow and cautious manner on the extreme left side of Raichur-Lingasugur road.

When he was near the petrol bunk, Kavital, respondent No.1 being the driver of the Tata Indica Vista Car bearing registration No.KA-36/TF-4631 ('offending vehicle' for short), came in a high speed in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
In the said accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries including fractures resulting in permanent partial disability.
Despite prolonged treatment he is not completely cured.

As the driver, owner and insurer of the offending vehicle,
respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Before the Tribunal respondent Nos.1 and 2 have remained absent and as such they are placed ex-parte.

5. Respondent No.3/Insurance company appeared through counsel and filed written statement disputing the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, accident and that the driver of the offending vehicle was responsible for the accident.
Respondent No.3 has specifically contended that at the time of alleged accident, petitioner was not holding a valid driving license and as such he was responsible for causing the accident.
Respondent No.1 was also not holding a valid driving license and as such it is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issued.

He has relied upon Ex.P1 to 145.
8.
On behalf of respondent No.3, one witness is examined as RW-1 and Ex.R1 to 5 are marked.
9. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.4,66,165/- with interest at 6% p.a.

It also held that at the time of accident, petitioner was not holding a valid driving license and as such contributed towards the cause of accident and determined the percentage of negligence at 25% and as such reduced the compensation by 25% and held that petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.3,49,624/- and directed respondent No.3 to pay the same with interest.

The details of the compensation granted by the Tribunal is as under:

 For Pain and suffering 30,000  For Medical expenses
2,04,765  For loss earnings during the period of 18,000  treatment for a period of three  months @ Rs.6,000/- p.m
For attendant charges 9,000  For special diet and nutrition food 10,000
For loss of future earning capacity due 1,94,400  to permanent physical disability  caused to the extent of 15% of whole  body of petitioner
TOTAL 4,66,165  75% of the compensation comes to 3,49,624 10.
Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
11. During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the impugned judgment and award is contrary to law and material evidence placed on record.

In the accident, the petitioner has sustained following two fractures:
(i) Type III open fracture shaft of Right Femur (ii) Comminuted fracture proximal tibia 11.1
Due to the above injuries, appellant took treatment as in-patient for 19 days.
He has undergone operation.
The injuries suffered by him has resulted in shortening of right leg about 2" inches and he has sustained 26% disability of the whole body.
However, the Tribunal has erred in considering the whole body disability at 15%.
He would further submit that the compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side.
No compensation is granted under the head loss of amenities of life.

sentences.text: 13. On the other hand, learned counsel representing respondent No.3 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.

14. Heard arguments and perused the record.
15.

Having regard to the fact that respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of (2018)SCCR 691 the Tribunal that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, petitioner sustained injuries has attained finality.

However, it is to be seen whether the Tribunal is justified in reducing the compensation by 25% on the ground that having not holding a valid driving license at the time of accident, petitioner has contributed 25% negligence towards the cause of the accident.
16. Undisputably the concerned police after conducting detailed investigation have filed charge sheet against respondent No.1, being the driver of the offending vehicle.

Had petitioner also contributed towards the cause of the accident, for the reason that he was not holding a valid driving license, certainly the Investigating Officer would have also arraigned him as accused.
Absolutely there is no evidence to show that petitioner also contributed towards the cause of accident.

In fact Ex.P2 which is spot mahazar also contains the sketch of the place of accident, which shows that at the time of accident, petitioner was proceeding on the left side of the road and it was respondent No.1 who caused the accident by steering towards his right side and dashing against the motor cycle on which the petitioner was proceeding.

Respondents have not examined respondent No.1 to establish that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the petitioner or at least he has contributed towards the cause of the accident.

17. In the absence of such evidence, the Tribunal has erred in relying upon the decisions in MFA.No.30284/2008 dated 05.12.2012, wherein on facts this Court has held that because the claimant therein was not holding a valid driving license he contributed towards the cause of accident.

Though in the present case, it is proved that the petitioner was not holding a valid driving license, however, there is no evidence to prove that petitioner contributed towards the cause of the accident,
especially for the reason that he was not holding a valid driving license.

In the absence of such evidence, the Tribunal has erred in relying upon the above decision and coming to the conclusion that in this case also there was 25% contributory negligence on the part of petitioner and as such he is not entitled for that much of the Venkanagouda @ Venkatesh S/O ... vs Prakash S/O Chandrashekar And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171445238/
4 compensation.

As held in Mangla Ram's case referred to supra, in a petition under the provisions of M.V.Act, the petitioner is required to prove his case on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and the Tribunal cannot expect him to prove his case beyond reasonable doubt and in the absence of convincing evidence regarding negligence on the part of the petitioner, compensation cannot be reduced on the ground of contributory negligence.

18. For the above reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that findings of the Tribunal that petitioner has contributed 25% negligence towards the cause of accident is liable to be set aside and as such he would be entitled for entire compensation.
19. Now coming to the quantum of compensation which the petitioner is entitled.
Based on the material placed on record, the Tribunal has correctly accepted the age of the petitioner as 24 years and as such the appropriate multiplier '18'.

In the absence of proof of exact income, having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2014, based on minimum wages, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.7,500/- instead of Rs.6,000/-p.m.
During the course of his evidence, PW-2 who has treated the petitioner has deposed that petitioner has sustained 26% disability of the lower limb.
In fact during his cross- examination he has admitted that the physical disability calculated by him was only with respect to the particular limb and not with respect to the whole body.
Therefore, the Tribunal is justified in taking the whole body disability at 15%.
Consequently, there is no justification for the petitioner to claim that the disability ought to have been taken at 26% of the whole body.
With these components, the compensation under the head loss of future earnings on account of disability is Rs.7,500 x 12 x 18 x 15% = Rs.2,43,000/- as against Rs.1,94,400/- granted by the Tribunal.
20. Based on the medical bills, the Tribunal has correctly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.2,04,765/- under the head medical expenses and it requires no interference.
21. Since the petitioner has suffered two fractures, in all probabilities, it would be expected that he was under treatment for a period of three months.

Therefore, at the rate of Rs.7,500/- p.m,
petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.22,500/- as against Rs.18,000/- granted by the Tribunal under the head loss of earning during the period of treatment.
22. Taking into consideration the nature of injury as well as the period of treatment, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.9,000/- under the head attendant charges.
However, compensation under the head special diet and nourishment is enhanced to Rs.15,000/- as against Rs.10,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head pain and sufferings.
However, it has not granted any compensation under the head loss of amenities of life.

Taking into consideration the fact that petitioner has suffered two fractures and was under treatment for a period of three months and also the injuries have resulted in permanent partial disability, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head pain and sufferings and Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of amenities of life.

5 23.
Thus, in all petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.5,64,265/- as against Rs.4,66,165/- quantified by the Tribunal.

Since he is entitled for entire compensation and the Tribunal is not justified in deducting 25% of the compensation, the compensation which the petitioner is entitled is enhanced to Rs.5,64,265/- as against Rs.3,49,624/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:
 Heads Amount granted Amount granted  by the Tribunal by this Court  In Rs. In Rs.
 For Pain and suffering 30,000 40,000  For Medical expenses 2,04,765 2,04,765

For loss earnings during 18,000 22,500  the period of treatment  for a period of three  months @ Rs.6,000/-
 p.m  For attendant charges 9,000 9,000  For special diet and 10,000 15,000  nutrition food

For loss of future 1,94,400 2,43,000  earning capacity due to  permanent physical  disability caused to the  extent of 15% of whole  body of petitioner  Loss of amenities of life - 30,000  TOTAL 4,66,165 5,64,265  75% of the 3,49,624  compensation comes to 24.
Of course, petitioner is entitled for interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
( i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.5,64,265/- as against Rs.3,49,624/-
granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% p.a on the enhanced compensation.
(iii) Respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation together with interest at 6% p.a within a period of six weeks from the date of order and recover the same from respondent No.1.
(iv) The registry is directed to send the trial Court record along with copy of this judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.
